90372.overview: In this game, the player controls Roger the Dodger (aka: Blagger), a burglar whose task is to collect a series of keys in a certain location, then use them to open the safe. There are 30 levels to be completed. Blagger must perform these tasks under a time limit while avoiding hazards such as cacti, cars, aliens, mad hatters, giant mouths, and chinamen. Blagger has no weapon to shoot these, but must rely on his jumping skills. He loses a life if he comes into contact with a hazard or falls long distances, or if he runs out of time. As usual, the game ends when all lives are lost. If Blagger successfully grabs the keys and makes his way to the safe, he proceeds to the next location.

90386.overview:
Bug Eyes 2: Starman to the Rescue is a video game developed by Scrooloose and Bitbrain and published in 1986 by Audiogenic Software, and re-released by Alternative Software.

Light years from Earth lies the rusting hulk of the Xxabanean flagship, disabled when its power generator was destroyed by Space Agent Zelda. But Zelda was captured and imprisoned in the depths of a distant and desolate asteroid. Somewhere hidden on the rusting ship are the 25 keys that are needed to free Zelda from her intergalactic prison.
Your mission, as Space Agent Starman, is to penetrate the defences of the ship and find the 25 keys in order to rescue Zelda. Some of the old Xxanabean booby traps are still in operation, and strange alien creatures have moved into the empty hulk.
You have only five refills of oxygen. Your limited supply is depleted more quickly by collisions with objects and creatures. You must find the key before it runs out.

90387.overview: Barbarian II: The Dungeon of Drax is a video game first published in 1988 for various home computers. It was also released as Axe of Rage in North America. The game is the sequel to Barbarian: The Ultimate Warrior (Death Sword in North America), which was published in 1987. In Barbarian II, the player controls a princess or barbarian character, exploring the game world to locate and defeat an evil wizard. The game's plot is an extension of its predecessor, although the gameplay is different. While the first game offers two players the opportunity for virtual head-to-head combat, the second is solely a single-player adventure with fewer fighting moves.

90449.overview:
A clone of Centipede where you must blast the centipede into oblivion before it reaches the base of the playing area and multiplies.

The centipede moves across the screen and when it reaches the other side it moves down one place and moves back across the screen. You control a spacecraft at the bottom of the screen shooting the Centipede whilst moving left or right as well, being able to move forwards and backwards a short distance. Shooting the Centipede a number of times splits it into two and the other parts split into two when shot a number of times.

Scattered around the screen are mushrooms and when the Centipede hits them then it changes directions, but the mushrooms can be shot to make them disappear and receive points. Other creatures make an appearance and need shooting or avoiding, and they are an insect that places more mushrooms, spiders, scorpions and snails and if you are touched by any creatures then you lose one of three lives. Destroying all parts of the Centipede moves you to the next level.

90512.overview:
Bruce Lee is a video game designed by Ron J. Fortier, with graphics by Kelly Day and music by John A. Fitzpatrick. It was originally developed in 1983 for the Atari 8-bit and published in 1984 for the Atari 8-bit and Commodore 64 by Datasoft Inc and for the BBC Micro, Amstrad CPC & ZX Spectrum by U.S. Gold.
The BBC port was done by Micro Power.

The aim is to reach a wizard in an underground lair, defeat of whom can offer untold wealth.
In each area you must collect the many strategically-placed lanterns before exiting through the newly-revealed passageway. Some rooms also have escalator-type sections to run along, and the standard (although slightly illogical in this context) ladders. There are 20 areas to be completed.
On the way, you'll fight two enemies - a ninja and a green sumo warrior named Yamo. You can defeat them by punching, kicking, dropping on their heads or luring them into hazardous terrain, or even by making them accidentally hit each other. Even after they are killed, however, they keep coming back for more after a few seconds. Since they can move pretty intelligently (they even climb ladders), you should watch out for them. The game also allows a second player to take control of Yamo.
There are lots of hazards to avoid by either walking round or jumping - walls of electrical charge and exploding bushes for example.

90562.overview: Barbarian: The Ultimate Warrior is a video game first released for Commodore 64 personal computers in 1987; the title was developed and published by Palace Software, and ported to other computers including the BBC Micro in the following months. The developers licensed the game to Epyx, who published it as Death Sword in the United States. Barbarian is a fighting game that gives players control over sword-wielding barbarians. In the game's two-player mode, players pit their characters against each other. Barbarian also has a single-player mode, in which the player's barbarian braves a series of challenges set by an evil wizard to rescue a princess.

90650.overview:
Bug Eyes is a video game published in 1985 by Icon.

You play Agent Starman, your job is to avoid the destruction of civilization and taking over the galaxy by the bug-eyed Xabanneus alien hordes. Penetrate the ten levels of the Mother ship and destroy the power generator. You carry on your back an oxygen supply (represented by the energy bar on top) and an alien repulsion mechanism that will sometimes activate in times of danger.

90786.overview:
Published by Firebird for the BBC Microcomputer.

Wing the planes to release a carrier pigeon, shoot the pigeon and add a note to the stave at the top of the screen. if you can complete the tune you will be rewarded with a bonus of 1500 points and move onto the next level.

Attacking planes will drop bombs and relentlessly home-in on your position at the bottom of the screen. Planes can only be destroyed by hitting them dead centre. If all the planes are destroyed but insufficient notes placed on the stave to complete the tune, your bonus is lost and you will be given a second chance.

90787.overview:
Developed by Martyn Howard and published by Superior Software in 1987 for the BBC Microcomputer.
A Repton style game.
The levels are filled with dirt (which vanishes when Bono walks over it), monsters and glooks (basically rocks with eyes). Monsters can only travel on ways without dirt and their touch is hazardous - some even eat up the skeletons. There are 25 skeletons to find in each level and specific steps have to be worked out to reach them (e.g. using a glook to cut off a specific monster's path) giving the game a puzzle-solving character. The game was also ported to Acorn Electron, Commodore 64, and Commodore Amiga.

91014.overview:
BMX on the Moon was programmed by Tim Tyler for the BBC Microcomputer. It was published by Superior Software in 1984.

In this game you control a Moon Cycle which you use to patrol the surface of the Moon. You must avoid the rocks on the surface and also the monsters bouncing high in the low gravity. You should try to shoot down the spaceships which fly overhead dropping bombs. A further hazard is the flying bombs which are often just too high to shoot or jump over, and just too low to squeeze underneath.

91015.overview:
Battle Planet is a 1-player arcade shooter for the BBC Micro.

Human civilization is threatened by the approach of alien Battle Planets, huge spaceships the size of planets than can destroy whole worlds. These seemingly invulnerable spaceships have one weakness, located in a trench on the planet's surface. The player's mission is to fly into the trench and launch a plasma bolt into the Battle Planet's heart.

Played from a perspective behind the spaceship, the player can move their ship left, right, up, and down, as well as shoot forwards. Oncoming Robot Fighters try to destroy the player. Ships that approach from the front must be avoided or shot, while only shields can protect the player from ships that approach from above. As the player approaches their target, the invincible commander ship approaches from behind to threaten the player.

91017.overview:
Ballistix was written by Peter Scott and published for the BBC Microcomputer by Superior Software in 1989.

Ballistix is an arcade game in which you have to manipulate a ball in order to score a goal with your opponent. To do this, you will control an arrow that defines a direction, and pressing the fire key will launch a ball from this arrow in the direction the arrow points to; by launching balls at correct angles, you will manipulate the main ball and control the way it moves. Ballistix also keeps certain physics laws (namely gravity and friction), and will present you with varying obstacles in either one or two player mode.

91111.overview:
Balloon Buster is a video game developed by Mike Williams and published for the BBC Microcomputer and Acorn Electron by Blue Ribbon.


Buster the clown likes to laugh, and what really bursts him is bursting balloons. As he is a little color-blind, help him get a highscore!

91117.overview:
3D Bomb Alley is a video game created by Software Invasion for the BBC Micro and Acorn Electron.
The player’s task is to shoot down the approaching bomber aircraft using the crosshairs. The ships on the water represent the player’s lives, and each bomb dropped destroys one of them. The player receives a new ship after scoring 300 points, and subsequent ships after a random number of points ranging between 250 and 400. As the game progresses, the number of approaching bombers increases, and the game ends when the player loses all their ships.

91127.overview:
Boffin is a platform game developed by Paul Julian O'Malley and published by Addictive Games.

The aim of Professor Boffin is to pass through a series of caves as quickly as possible by destroying all of the unlucky horseshoes in each cavern and then touching the resident owl, guardian of each cave.

There are two different versions of Boffin on the tape. Boffin v.2 is recorded first, followed by v.1. Boffin v.2 runs on the Acorn Electron and also the BBC Micro. It has 25 different caverns. The first version of Boffin runs on the BBC Micro and features high resolution graphics and 20 caverns - all completely different from those in Boffin v.2.

91132.overview:
Blast! was developed by Sam Inglis and released by Audiogenic Software (ASL) for the BBC Microcomputer in 1989.
You are in control of a floating space ship, a bit like the one from Thrust, but much smaller on the screen. You have to blast your way through everything that moves on the screen. When you have blown up everything, you move on to the next level. You have to balance the ship and stop it from smashing into any aliens/walls as well as firing.

91190.overview:
Bounty Bob Strikes Back! is the sequel to Miner 2049er and features similar gameplay. As Bounty Bob, your goal is to claim every inch of 25 challenging mines. To do this, you must walk over each segment of the framework in the mines. To reach each segment of framework, you will need to figure out a way to jump, climb, or use one of the many devices occasionally available to get there. To your help you get around (or sometimes hinder progress) are ladders, slides, suction tubes, cannons, transporters, and other devices. Wandering about the mines are many dangerous mutants. If you come in contact with one of these, you will lose a life. Scattered throughout each mine are special food items; collect one of these, and you will temporarily be able to eliminate the mutants by walking into them. You will need to figure out a unique strategy for each level in order to complete it, plus there is a time limit so claim all the territory quickly!

The BBC Micro version was developed by Paul Johnson for Micro Power, and published by U.S. Gold.

91192.overview:
Boulder Dash is a video game developed by First Star Software and released for a number of home computers. The BBC Microcomputer version was published by Tynesoft in 1988.

You are Rockford, and you have to dig through monster infested caves in search of diamonds. In each level you must collect a certain number of these diamonds, in order to open a portal to the next stage. Enemies can be squashed by falling boulders, which are released when the ground below them is removed or they are pushed onto empty ground, but be careful because these can also squash you. In later levels, difficulty is increased by many puzzle elements and shorter time limits.
There are 16 levels to be completed and five different skill levels available, which affect the number of jewels which must be collected and the time limit.

91439.overview:
Breakthrough (or Break Through) is a game for the BBC Microcomputer, developed by Ian Collinson and published by Audiogenic Software (ASL).
A puzzle game similar in style to Solomon's Key, in which you have to place blocks and melt them in order to get to the keys hidden somewhere on the screen.

91442.overview: Bumble Bee is a top view single screen maze game where you play the role of a bee and you have to collect all the pollen on the screen to move to a box marked OUT to go to the next level. There are two types of walls on the screen and they are red and yellow with red walls able to be turned to pass through them while yellow walls are solid and cannot be moved. As you move around the screen there are toadstools and fireballs which must be avoided but there are points to collect for bonuses. A bar moves along the right, bottom and left of the screen and when it reaches the top of the left side then a spider appears. The spider has to be avoided but he can't turn the red walls so you can make him hit the fireballs to kill them, but toadstools have no effect. The bar grows again when the spider appears and when it reaches the left again then another spider appears. If you touch a spider, toadstool or fireball then you lose one of three lives.

91445.overview:
Boxer is a platform game written by Wal Mansell. It was released for the BBC Microcomputer by Acornsoft.

You and your computer controlled rival are competing for the attentions of a young lady. At the bottom of the screen, she is releasing balloons which you must try to catch when they get stuck in the rafters of the Gym. Any balloons which escape to the top of the screen will be awarded to your opponent.
If you collect five balloons before your opponent does, your score will be increased by the bonus in the top right-hand corner of the screen, and you will move to a more challenging Gym. If your opponent is the first one to collect five balloons, you will lose a life and stay in the same Gym.
You can only catch balloons safely while they are caught in the rafters. If you try to grab or touch one while it is moving you will fall over. This will also happen if you have contact with your opponent or any of the boxing gloves, hammers or dumb-bells which move across the Gym.
Every time you get three falls, you will lose a life. Gloves and hammers can be punched and dumb-bells jumped over to score points. Points can also be scored by jumping up to the punch balls at the bottom of the screen.

95716.overview: Bouncer is a clone of the Mlystar Electronics classic arcade game Q*Bert, which was developed and published by Acornsoft for the BBC Microcomputer in 1984.

95751.overview:
Bananaman is an action game that was developed and published by MRM Software for the BBC Microcomputer in 1983.

The player controls the Bananaman character, whose objective is to eat 40 banana sandwiches in under a minute. Randomly generated amounts of bonus points are awarded for eating the peeled bananas and eliminating Ethel the Cat when she appears. However, if he stands on a spider, runs out of time or gets completely surrounded by blue blocks, Bananaman will lose a life and the amount of banana sandwiches eaten on the current level will be reset.

96194.overview:
Blitzkrieg is a tank battle game released by Software Invasion for both the BBC Microcomputer and Acorn Electron.

Your gun turret is a fixed view at the bottom - the turret also recoils realistically when fired. On moving right and left, the landscape in the distance, which is at the top of the screen, scrolls to simulate the view from your cockpit. In the mid-view are the other enemy tanks which are you combatants in this game.

They appear at various distances and move in real time, in a manner relative to the landscape, whether you are scrolling it or not. If they stop and turn towards you, you need move quickly if you want to avoid their deadly shells. Shells that you fire take longer to reach more distant tanks and the sound of them blowing up is also diminished with extra distance. A tank that is more distant scores more, also as your score progresses, you get promoted to increasing military ranks.

98581.overview:
Blockbuster is a QBert style puzzle game created by Max Taylor, and developed and published by Micro Power.

Move Buster the rabbit over blocks to change them to the target colour. Only the red objects are safe to touch. Use spinning discs to lure the fox to it's death. Beware of the bird and it's noxious guano.

98827.overview:
B.C. Bill was developed by Creative Technology Group and released by Imagine for a range of home computers including the BBC Microcomputer.

As the caveman Bill, you must compete with other contemporary species, such as the dinosaurs, to collect food. Whack the food with your club and drag the food back to your cave before a dinosaur eats it – or you. But food alone is not enough for survival, you must also hunt cave-wives to secure your offspring. The procedure is the same here: hit the women with your club before they're eaten by a dinosaur, and drag them by their hair back to the cave (remember this was 1984). Your score is calculated according to how many seasons you've survived, how many wives and how much offspring you have.

112006.overview: Battlefields is a strategy game written by Ian Trackman. It features two historic arenas; the American Civil War and the Battle of Waterloo.

113543.overview: Black Queen is a contract bridge program both for beginners and for club players who wish to practice and improve their game. It was written by Michael Fellows.

124440.overview: Move along the blocks, avoiding the TNT while picking up the detonators. Make sure not to block your way to a detonator as the blocks disintegrate after you have stepped on them. Avoid the BOOT at all costs.

125004.overview: Atlantis is an underwater version of the arcade game Scramble in which you have to move past a right to left scrolling underwater landscape avoiding, shooting or bombing mines, obstacles and missiles.

125629.overview: Bubble Bobble is a platform game, with each level being a single screen. The enemies must be cleared from a level to go to the next one. With one player controlling Bub and the other controlling Bob, the player can jump and collect items for points (such as fruit). The real power Bub and Bob have however is the ability to blow bubbles. These bubbles can be as platforms to leap on, or to trap enemies. Enemies trapped in a bubble must be popped by jumping into them, wherein they'll turn to fruit. Additionally, power-ups sometimes float by in bubbles. They include lightning, which flies out horizontally at enemies, and water, which drags the player and enemies straight down flowing over platforms. Taking too long to complete any level will summon Baron Von Blubba, who will float around the screen trying to destroy the player

125649.overview:
Buffalo Bill's Wild West Show (known as Buffalo Bill's Rodeo Games in Europe) is a collection of six Wild West themed mini-games. You can play as many or as few of these as you like, and can always have another go at them if you fail.
Games include Knife Throwing, Trick Shooting, Calf Roping and Bronco Riding.

The games were programmed by Kevin Blake and Jason Sobell. The original 1989 release was by Tynesoft with a re-release in 1992 by Microvalue.

125670.overview:
Brian Clough's Football Fortunes is a football management computer board game suitable for two to five players.

Each player takes on the role of a club manager. The object of the game is for each manager to successfully steer his team through the season using his skill to make his team stronger as the game proceeds. Each manager competes with human and computer controlled teams in a ten strong league and the F.A. Cup. From the second season onwards, each team will also enter a European competition (League Champions to the European Cup, F.A. Cup Winners to the Cup-Winners’ Cup, and the remaining clubs will go to the UEFA Cup).

The winner of Brian Clough's Football Fortunes is the manager who survives to the end of the game and has the highest number of game points. Game points are points awarded by the computer program, based on each managers performance in League and Cup competitions and on the amount of cash the player has left at the end of the game.

127032.overview:
Battle 1917 is a turn-based strategy game for one or two players. The game background is World War I with its new technology and the first use of tanks. Players command 29 units of five types: infantry, cavalry, tanks, artillery and a king. The object of the game, like in chess, is to kill the enemy king who is the weakest and slowest piece on the board. Each unit has different stats. 

The map is 21x32 squares large and is randomly generated for every new game. Objects on the map include wires, forests, rivers and units. 

The game was programmed by Mark Lucas for the Sinclair Spectrum and converted to the BBC Micro by P Martin. 

Mark Lucas won the 1983 Cambridge Award for Battle 1917.

127076.overview:
Eddie Murphy became a star in the police film Beverly Hills Cop, and it was this license that Tynesoft used to create a game featuring four distinct sub-games, each of which can be practiced from the main screen in some versions. First Axel Foley visits a warehouse to shoot out some bad guys in a Green Beret-influenced sequence.



The second level (first on the C64 version) involves driving after 3 lorries full of weapons, and shooting them out one by one, Chase HQ-style. Avoid contact and stay on the road to complete this. Next you must cross the grounds of a mansion, shooting anyone who gets in your way.



The final section is set within the mansion, and is first-person 3D, although with few movement angles and only one enemy on screen at a time.

132820.overview:
A dictator took the control of a fortress on the island of Kuhn-Lin.

The player's mission is to storm the island and recapture it. This takes place over the course of six different sequences. The first sequence is Aerial Reconnaissance, where the fleet must be moved directly past the enemy or into a hidden passage to trigger another, optional stage. In this Hidden Passage sequence, the player will have to maneuver around mines and torpedoes. Successfully completing it gives a surprise advantage in the following General Quarters sequence, where the player controls anti-aircraft guns shooting down enemy aircraft.

The next sequence is named Battle Stations and the player must aim and fire heavy guns to hit enemy ships before they inflict too much damage and eventually sink the player's own vessels. Following this battle, the fleet must be maneuvered to the beach. Upon reaching the Beach-Head level, tanks roll out and the player must keep these safe from enemy fire and obstacles while driving. In the Final Battle sequence, the Dictator is holed up in the fortress of Kuhn-Lin and 10 different targets on the fortress must be fired upon to destroy it.

The port for C16 and Plus/4 computers only contains the General Quarters, Battle Stations and Final Battle sequences.

134693.overview:
The Great Ring needs to be returned to Mount Doom, a treacherous task to be undertaken by Fordo the Boggit. Spam, Pimply and Murky are his country-bumpkin friends, and he will later meet with Bumbadil and Hashberry, two old hippies. The main quest involves meeting up with Legoland the Elf, Giblet the Dwarf and Aragont.
In keeping with the humour, familiar locations become "the featureless plain below the pink mountain", "Lake Anadin" and the "Land of the Personal-Stereo-Wearing Goblins".

Bored of the Rings is an interactive fiction game with graphics made using Quill. It was written by Fergus McNeill and Ian Willis. The interface allows the player to take and use items using VERB NOUN commands, and talk to characters.
The game is split into three parts, accessed via passcodes. The tape also includes issue 1 of Sceptical, Delta 4's short-lived magazine on tape.

135080.overview: As the renowned pilot "Baron Von Rippoffen", it is your duty to destroy the enemy landscape. Loaded with bombs, your plane will fly over the cities. It's up to you to destroy them completely and land, thus paving the way for reinforcements.

135268.overview:
A Space Invaders variant in which you are attacked by Swoopers, Kamakazee Birds and Death Bombs.
The birds start off in formation, with Swoopers peeling off and attacking, bombing you as they circle.
Kamakazee Birds also peel off and home in on you. If they miss they then re-appear at the screen top.
You are also attacked by Death Bombs which you must shoot before they reach the bottom, otherwise you lose a life.
You start with three lives and gain a bonus one every fourth time that you clear a screen.

135316.overview:
This is a graphical adventure in which you play the part of Zorakk and take control of his loyal warriors. Your quest is to obtain the three parts to the crown of Ultimate Darkness. Each part of the crown is located in each of the three lands of Ramagold; Lannia - a greenland, Durnin - a desertland and Zarthynia - an iceland. In each land are four buildings; a Bazaar, a Sanctuary, a Tomb and a Ruin.

Bazaar
Essentially a shop where you can use gold to purchase more warriors or food.

Sanctuary
If during the course of a game, your Warrior, Gold or Food levels fall below an acceptable level, you may enter the sanctuary.

Tomb and Ruin
These are battle arenas. Their role in the adventure is the same except only one contains the part of the crown. Do not enter either of these unless you consider you have sufficient warriors to do battle. 

Rewards are only obtained after defeating a number of Brigands in a battle. Any one of the following can be given as a reward: Warriors, Gold, Food, a Map, a Dragon Sword, a Magic Potion, a Piece of the Crown.

The game was unknowingly re-released in 1986 as Bozo The Brave by Tynesoft.

135650.overview:
This is a wargame of the 21st Century in which you have control of the forces opposing a single enemy unit known as the Ogre. There are ten levels of play.

Your mission is to stop the Ogre from leaving the bottom of the map. The only way to do this is to destroy all its tread units. The Ogre itself is a computer-controlled supertank, which is bristling with weapons. It has missile systems, main and secondary batteries as well as a host of anti-personnel weapons. The Ogre is a tread or track vehicle, and the number of "squares" it is able to move in any one turn is governed by the number of tread units divided by 15.

Under your command, you have a number of different units: Command Post and Howitzer both of which are fixed, and Ground Effect Vehicle, Heavy Tank, Missile Tank and Infantry which are all mobile. 	  	  	  	 

Before play begins, you will be shown what units are available to you and how many of each you have. If you are not satisfied with the mixture of units provided, you may change them.
The map, with craters and the Ogre in position will then be displayed and you will be asked which level of difficulty (1-10).
Next, all your units will also be displayed, in position, on the map, and you must decide who moves first.

Having decided who goes first, the Ogre's current status will appear on the bottom line.
ML (number of Missiles left)
MB (number of main batteries)
SB (number of secondary batteries)
AP (number of anti-personnel weapons)
TR (number of tread units remaining)

136230.overview: In this war simulation based on the WWII Battle of Britain you take control of the Royal Air Force, Fighter Command while the computer controls the Luftwaffe.

138373.overview:
Danger UXB is a variant of the arcade game Check Man. The player moves over a grid of squares and has to reach bombs before their counters reach zero and then explode. Each square can be moved over only once and thereafter it disappears. It is however possible to slide rows left and right and new squares will then appear. In addition to the bombs there are flags that can be collected and lethal skulls which have to be avoided.

There are three difficulty levels. On the second level the bombs have shorter countdowns and on the third level the stamping boots from the arcade game appear. Theses wander around the grid and will kill the player upon contact.

138466.overview: A computer game version of a famed TV quiz show based around the game of darts. The computer version features 2 players, both human-controlled - on TV there were 3 teams of 2 (one amateur darts player and one to answer questions).

146738.overview: All fights take place to realistic WBA rules, as you aim to rise the rankings and fight for the title. The crowd frequently shout encouragement and insults, which are displayed using speech bubbles. You need to wait until the referee is not looking in order to perform illegal moves such as kicks and groin punches. Fights last 15 rounds, and a knockout ends that round, not the entire fight. The game was re-released in 1990 by Codemasters under the name Pro Boxing Simulator.

150752.overview:
Two strategy games for up to four players.
In Black Box, four atoms are hidden within an eight by eight grid. The object of the game is to deduce the exact position of the atoms by examining the paths taken by rays fired into the grid.
The object of Gambit is for each player to attempt to be the first to get all of their four men back to the central home area. Players position walls to direct their own men home or to block their opponents and can send a man back to the start by running over him.

152901.overview:
Bandits At 3 O' Clock is a one or two player game for joysticks only. The one player game allows you to perfect your dogfighting technique by chasing and shooting the computer-controlled plane. The plane is controlled using the joystick. Pulling the joystick back (down) will make the plane climb; pushing forward (up) will make it dive and pushing the joystick to the side will make the plane increase speed. 
The option menu allows you to select 1 or 2 players, the background (day or night), clouds, flak and air-ships. A plane cannot be shot down when it is in the cloud but it can crash into the other plane. Either plane can be shot down by flak and if the player flies too close to the enemy airship it will be fired at. 
If the planes fly into the red at the top of the screen they will be prone to stall.

152925.overview:
Barrage is a turn based artillery game for two player. Each player is in control of a gun and has to shoot projectiles at the other. In each battle there are 100 men on each side and the aim is to kill all of the enemies' men. On the screen there are also two cities which have to be avoided since hitting them leads to penalties. The landscape is generated for each new game and during the game it is redrawn as shots create craters in the ground.
The game is keyboard controlled and each player has to enter values for the angle and the velocity of the shot while taking into account the wind speed and direction. Players with more than 35 men in their army will also be asked to set a delta angle and velocity which decides if shots will be spread out or fired in a tight cluster. The number of shots taken depends on how many men the player has left.

152926.overview:
Up to six players can start the game and, after entering the names of the players and a minimum bet level, you must choose the number of meetings that the game will be played over. Each meeting consists of six races. 
When the game starts, the form and odds for each horse in the race will be displayed and each player must choose a horse and the amount of the bet. When all bets are placed, the race will start. The game ends when either all the meetings have taken place or one of the players reaches the target amount of money.

152927.overview:
You are a tank gunner and your task is to shoot the enemy tank before it shoots you. However, your mission does not finish there asthere will be other tanks. 
A scanner is displayed in the bottom right-hand corner of the screen. This shows the position of the enemy tank relative to you. You can then turn to get the tank in view. The next stage is to position the tank in the rectangular viewfinder by fine adjustments of your controls.

152971.overview:
A compilation of seven games from Audiogenic Software: 

•   Psycastria
•   Thunderstruck
•   Ultron
•   Contraption
•   Wizzy's Mansion
•   Space Ranger
•   Last of the Free

152972.overview: Evil demons from the Underworld have ransacked Boris's home and carried off his valuables. Playing as Boris, you must journey to the Underworld and retrieve your possessions. Whenever you defeat a demon, one of your valuables will appear and you can collect it. Touching the walls of the Underworld results in instant death. Disks also appear and they cannot be destroyed.

162040.overview: A well made Tetris clone written in 1991 by Charles Reilly.  However, he had forgotten about it and released it as public domain (with some tweaking to the code) in 2017.

168284.overview:
Boffin 2 is a platform game developed by Paul Julian O'Malley and published by Addictive Games. Like the original, the aim of Professor Boffin is to pass through a series of caves as quickly as possible by destroying all of the unlucky horseshoes in each cavern and then touching the resident owl, guardian of each cave.

Boffin 2 is included in the original Boffin release and is essentially the same game but all 25 screens have been updated to new layouts.

177678.overview: Bar Billiards is a fun pub sport widely played across the South of England and in the Channel Islands. A Bar Billiards table is similar to a small Billiards table and comes with seven white balls and one red ball. Instead of pockets, holes are sunk into the table; 5 in a row across the far end of the table and four set in a diamond pattern in the rear half of the table. The nearest hole to the front, worth 200 points, has a black skittle in front of it which must not be toppled. Next up are two holes near the sides of the table that are each worth 50 points. Then there is a hole worth 100 points in the middle of the table. The holes across the end of the table score 30, 20, 10, 20 and 30 respectively. Finally, there is a spot in front of the 200 hole for the red ball and a baulk line across the width of the table near the front with a small D extending forwards from it.

177679.overview:
Golf is a 1-player sports game for multiple systems.

Played from a top-down perspective, the player chooses the club, angle, and power of their shot. Wind factors into ball movement, and the golfer must contend with sand traps and water hazards. After landing on the green, the game enters putting mode where the player can sink their ball. The game tracks score over multiple hole

177691.overview:
Game description:

In the year 2184 men were sent down into earth to wander the electronic grids that supply the human cities. However, giant bugs made it hard. You play as Henry who is one of the men that tried to get rid of the bugs.

You shoot out bombs that bounce left and right or up and down. Those bombs can destroy you, so better watch out. Also you can not shoot more than 3 bombs at a time

205961.overview:
The King, on hearing news that his old friend the wizard had been imprisoned by the evil Baron, sends an army forth to rescue him. The young Prince Jason was left behind, but eager to help, he took a short cut and landed in trouble inside the Baron's forbidding castle.
The wizard can be rescued by finding four objects belonging to him (Book of Spells, Wand, Crystal Ball and Ring) and taking them to his cell. There are 133 screens with 49 objects. You can carry only two objects at a time and the objects can only be dropped on the coloured bases, You must also get past various animals and the guards.

205977.overview:
Bozo and Beebo is an arcade game heavily inspired by the arcade game Clowns/Circus.

The goal is to pop all balloons with Bobo or Beebo. If one of them is in the air the player can move them left or right. If one of them misses the rocker he will die.

206003.overview: All you have to do is stop the People Eaters chasing you around the screen by placing obstacles in their way. Sounds simple, doesn't it? But "Brick 'em in".... OR ELSE!

206004.overview:
Britain's No. 1 Football Management Game Four Divisions FA Cup European Cup Cup Winners' Cup Full Game Save Ever fancied yourself as the Manager of a Football team? Ever thought "Why did they buy him?" or "He's a useless manager, I could do better than that!"? Well, now's your chance. Test your decision making and managerial skills with Alternative Software's Football Management game Soccer Boss.

"Soccer Boss" is a re-issue of the 1984 Peaksoft title "The Boss", both titles being identical in-game.
The game was originally written for the Dragon 32 by Harry Whitehouse and converted to the BBC Micro by Gordon Smith.

206291.overview: Not to be confused with the war strategy of the same name, Battle of Britain by Betasoft is also based on the famous World War II battle, but this is a flight combat simulation. The game was developed by Philip Coulson an published in 1985.

206321.overview:
This is a multi-event sports game licensed by British judoka and 1972 Olympic bronze medallist Brian Jacks and loosely based on the BBC sports programme Superstars. In this game you compete against Brian in eight different events and you score points in these events based on your performance. The events are Running, Archery, Cycling, Football, Swimming, Squat Thrusts, Canoeing and Arm Dips. There is no qualification time/score to beat, and you compete in all events regardless of performance. The game plays in a number of levels and should you score more points than Brian you win the level and move onto the next one where the process is repeated. Afterwards the scores from each level are combined for a total score, should Brian score more points than you at the end of any level then you will lose the challenge.

Also released as part of 10 Computer Hits 3 (Beau Jolly)

206322.overview: Breakout is a clone of the arcade game of the same name for the BBC Micro . This version was developed by Chris Melville and published by IPC Electrical-Electronic Press in Your Computer magazine, volume 3, issue 5, in May 1983.

206323.overview: Beebout is a homebrew clone of Super Breakout for the BBC Micro. It was developed by Simon Hooper and published by public domain label Retro Software in 2015.

206369.overview:
BBC Chess (also known as Beeb Chess, and Bug-Byte Chess) is Bug-Byte Software's attempt at an early computerized chess game for the BBC Micro. This version was released in 1982.

It is single-player only.

206424.overview: Compete against eight increasingly more aggressive opponents in this unique boxing simulation which stretches your computer to the limits. Super size sprites, superb animation and a touch of humour make this a game not to be missed. One or two players. Keyboard/joystick.

206571.overview: Bridge to the East combines arcade-style gameplay with text adventure. Players assume the role of a wizard tasked with protecting a group of heroes on a quest to restore the Crystals of Power. The game alternates between action sequences, where players collect crystals and defend a central structure from various threats, and adventure segments that present riddles to solve through text input.

206588.overview: Brainstorm is a two player game in which each player attempts to deflect his high energy laser beam into his opponent's 'brain' using light prisms which can be set to deflect the lasers in any one of eight directions.

206598.overview: Bridge Challenge is LiveWire Software's computerized version of the rather complex trick taking strategical card game, Bridge. It was released in 1984 for both the Acorn BBC Micro and The Acorn Electron.

206682.overview: Full flight simulation was offered in this innovative early release. Landing at night, you must take off, climb, control the plane mid air, and then land successfully. As well as basic steering, rudders, flaps, wheels and airspeed come under your control. There are five different flight challenges featured, including navigation as well as flight skills, plus a rolling demo on startup. A full instrument panel is provided for each of these, allowing you to judge speeds and distances.

206960.overview:
Published on the Fast Access disc, volume 2, issue 3, in 1990.

You must get back all the money in the mine. It sounds easy, but you must also look out for the cops and there is a time limit. Good luck!

207026.overview: Bandit is an unreleased title from Acornsoft. It is a clone of the 1979 arcade game Cosmic Guerilla from Universal.

207188.overview: The aim of the game is to guide a blue bee called Hank through a series of mazes to his hive while avoiding the spiders, insecticide cans, toadstools, and bee-eating lizards. Lost energy can be refreshed by picking up pollen, apples, flowers or honey.

216935.overview: A very early (and somewhat unusual) golf game.  While you have control of the choice of golf club and strength with which you'll hit the ball, you're not in control of the direction of where you want the ball to land.

216940.overview:
Beebmunch is a Pac-Man clone in which you have to eat all dots and avoid the ghosts (although after eating a power-up you can eat them, too).
You can eat fruits for bonus points.

218185.overview:
Bandits is a computer game for the BBC Micro platform, published by the slightly obscure Oak concern. It should not be confused with the very similarly named "Bandit" game put out by Acornsoft.
It's a variation of Asteroids, where you control a ship which can be rotated, thrust forward or jumped in hyperpace.

218186.overview:
It's a clone of the 1976 arcade classic Breakout from Atari.
This version can be found on the Arcade Action compilation from Acornsoft.

218187.overview: Breakout is a clone of the Atari arcade classic of the same name. This version was published by IJK Software. It was released only as part of a compilation pack.

218202.overview: A "Simon" game, wrote by Chris Wheater in 1981 with 14 years.

218203.overview:
Bobby Charlton Soccer is a 1–2 player soccer game for the BBC Micro and Electron.

At the beginning of each game, players take on the role of manager, and set the stamina, skill, and accuracy of each of their 11 players. These can be ranked 1–5 for each player, and the total skill for all 11 players must not equal more than 99. The player then sets the time for each half, their player positions on the field, color, who goes first, and whether there will be a computer opponent.

During the match, the playing field is displayed over three separate screens from a side view. The player can individually move one of their players, usually the player with the ball if their team has it. The player can move in the four cardinal directions, and shoot. The player at any time can switch their active player on the field. Players can receive injuries during game play, and the ball can be lost of the player reverses direction too quickly. Standard rules for a ball out-of-play apply.

218724.overview:
Beeb-Darts (also known as Flights of Fancy) is a 1-2 player darts game for the BBC Micro. It was developed by M.J. Parrot and published as a type-in game in the following:

-   Your Computer magazine, volume 3, issue 5, in May 1983.

-   Your Computer magazine, volume 6, issue 5, in May 1986.

419218.overview:
Braz is a platform game written by Paul Branton for Livewire in 1984. You play as Braz who has taken a job in a laboratory on the exact night a rogue and sinister bacteria is infecting all the chemicals stored around you. You must recover a set number of keys to quarantine it.
The game is something of a cross between Blagger and Woks in its idea of collecting keys and progressing through screens. However, it also has an element of arcade adventure in that you do not need to complete screens in a set order - you can traverse quite a large map, discovering and collecting keys in each room. Although you're only told to collect the keys, the game proper also tells you to look out for diamonds, gold, spades and umbrellas. What use these are you will have to discover for yourself.

Braz was initially developed to the box artwork packaging stage and was due for release in 1988 but was shelved.
The game itself was later recovered from the original cassette and was eventually published in 2002.

419320.overview:
A machine code arcade adventure for the BBC Micro.
Legend has it that any bear intelligent enough to reach the Inner Sanctum of the Golden Temple shall become Lord of the Lands of Mystery. Will Banjax prove to be such a bear?
If Banjax is killed he will be reincarnated at the last position you saved the screen. Use RETURN to save the screen.

419534.overview: Whilst in search of the treasure of the Great Skull Temple, Blizzard is confronted by his mutinous crew who are set on taking the booty for themselves. The Captain is forced to draw upon his iron will, calm intellect, skilful seamanship and devious resourcefulness to evade the frenzied sailors and claim the treasure as his own.

419779.overview:
Blockade puts you at the periscope of a submarine with orders to sink all enemy shipping.

Note:
Betasoft released a sister game titled Subhunt which reverses the roles, whereby you are the captain of a destroyer seeking out and attacking an enemy submarine.

419856.overview:
A real time advanced Star Trek game with extra facilities including probe satellites, damage reports and on-board computer.
Also released by Epsilon Software.

419870.overview: According to legend, somewhere there lies a fabulous treasure guarded by a ferocious Blue Dragon. Your quest in this adventure game is to find the treasure and avoid a fiery end, but first you must journey far into an unknown land where death may be your only reward.

420085.overview:
The idea is that you are a worker in a bun factory. Cakes pass in front of you on a conveyor belt and it's your job to put on the icing. Your mate further along the belt puts on the walnuts and you get paid piece-work. The more perfect cakes you make the more you earn. The more you waste the less you take home.
Sadly, your mate has just cleared off to do some fishing and you're left to do both the icing and the walnuts. You mustn't make too much mess or the machine will jam.

420192.overview: Your spaceship has to avoid or shoot a whole host of aliens of various formats which swirl, drop, crawl or wriggle across the screen.

420194.overview: A side -scrolling shooter. Referred to by it's short name of Scramble on the boxart spine, it was known by it's full title of Bomber Scramble in-game.

421732.overview:
Collect all the teapots then ring your friends for a cup of tea before your bonus reaches zero.
You score 50 points per teapot plus 20 points for each barrel you jump cleanly.

421889.overview: Boot Hill is a Wild West-themed arcade shooter for two players where the goal is to shoot your opposition. Players start from the opposite side of the screens, with the river between them. The game is a clone of the 1970s arcade classic of the same name.

422252.overview:
You are the commander of a small harbour in Cornwall when you are attacked by a squadron of Fokker bi-planes. Your only armament is an ancient Boer war cannon.

Known by it's full title on the boxart and in-game as just Harbour Command, this game was featured on the cassette bundled with the Micro User, vol. 3, issue 6, in August 1985.
It was also available to download from the BBC Ceefax service in September 1988.

422521.overview:
Beebchase (also known as Beeb Chase) is a 2023 homebrew port/clone of the Sinclair ZX Spectrum classic Deathchase for the BBC Micro. It was developed by Chirs Bradburne and released into the public domain in 2023.

Game description:

Deathchase sees you riding a motorcycle through 14 stages, with the aim of shooting out a succession of riders. Each stage starts with 2 bikes to shoot out, although planes and tanks also appear on the horizon, to be shot for bonus points. You start with 3 bikes and an infinite supply of bullets, with one bike lost every time you crash.

The levels are tree-lined, and at top speed it can be terrifying as you try to muscle through the gaps so as not to lose distance on the target bike. Every second level is played out at night, which changes the colour scheme. There are 14 levels to complete.

423848.overview: This is an unofficial conversion of the Atari arcade game for the BBC Micro. It was developed by Rocketeer and released into the public domain in 2023.

423900.overview:
Blockbusters is an adaptation for the BBC Micro of the game show of the same name.

Players answer questions to form a connection of colored cells either across the board, or from top to bottom, depending on whether they are playing as red or white.

The game was also published under the same title in 1988 by TV Games, a software label of Domark. The box cover featured a somewhat older Bob Holness.

425066.overview:
A compilation of ten games and two utilities, published by the Dutch software house Big Ben Club.
Calcsheet, Caterpillar, Cellars, Data Storage, Dominoes, Easter Mania, Froglet, Galgje (Hangman), Grijpertje (Cycles), Othello, Skypilot, Snakes And Ladders.

Note:
The box back mentions the game Veerman (Ferryman), but it's missing from the games menu.

439049.overview: This was the feature game on the Micro User cassette, volume 3, issue 7, in September 1985.

448748.overview: Beebgammon is a digital adaptation of the traditional backgammon game, where two players compete to move all their checkers off the board before their opponent.

456550.overview: Published as part of the Beebug magazine subscribers’ disc, "Blackjack" features a card game that's not blackjack. At the beginning of each game, seven cards are dealt to both players. One card is played to the table and players then proceed on playing cards on top it; only the same or higher rank can be played, otherwise player picks up the pile. The winner is whoever gets rid of their cards first.

456551.overview: Software Invasion's take on Blackjack doesn't differ from the standard formula; the objective is to achieve a hand value as close to 21 as possible without exceeding it, while also beating the dealer's hand.

456553.overview:
Bed Bugs is a shooter game set on a bed where the player defends against fleas and bed bugs that move from the top of the screen to bite at the bottom.

Players control a character in a top-down view, using false teeth or a jam sandwich to defeat the bugs. False teeth can bite the player’s toes if used at the bottom, and the jam sandwich leaves stains that a sponge can clean. A telephone lets the player call for help when overwhelmed. The game ends if the player is bitten eight times by a flea, once by a bed bug, moves off the bottom of the screen, or hits jam stains three times.

456556.overview:
Blue Ribbon Games Disk No. 2 is a compilation game featuring a collection of action, puzzle, and sports titles originally developed by MRM Software for the BBC Micro. The disk includes five games:

Screwball is an action-platform game where players navigate a ball or character through tricky terrain, avoiding obstacles to reach a goal.
Darts is a sports simulation game where players aim and throw darts at a virtual board, competing for high scores through precision and timing.
Q*Man's Brother is an action game inspired by QMan* (a Pac-Man clone), where players control a character collecting items in a maze while evading enemies.
Diamond Mine is a puzzle-action game where players dig through a grid to collect gems, avoiding cave-ins or enemies that can end the game.
Guy in the Hat is an action-adventure game featuring a hatted protagonist, likely centered on exploration or evasion through various levels.

456562.overview: Domark's Blockbusters is the second quiz game for the platform based on the game show of the same name. Players answer trivia questions to progress across a game board, aiming to connect a path from one side to the other. The game supports both single-player and two-player modes, allowing for competitive play. The digital adaptation maintains the format of the TV show, offering a variety of questions across multiple subjects.

456568.overview:
Bismarck is a strategic wargame set during World War II, where players control the Allied forces in a mission to destroy the German battleship Bismarck while protecting five convoys in the North Atlantic. Players command a variety of ships, including battleships, aircraft carriers, cruisers, and submarines, while tracking down the fast and evasive Bismarck, aided by the heavy cruiser Prinz Eugen.

The game offers both single-player and two-player modes, with the latter allowing one player to control the German forces. Players must manage resources, plan strategies, and engage in tactical decision-making. Victory can be achieved by sinking the Bismarck or earning points for destroying enemy ships and escorting convoys to safety.

456571.overview:
Blue Ribbon launched as a budget label in 1985, primarily reissuing MRM Software’s back catalog. This disk, being labeled "No. 1"  marked an early compilation effort shortly after the label’s inception, aligning with their initial focus on BBC Micro titles.

Games Featured:
Nightmare Maze - A maze-based game where players navigate a character through a series of increasingly complex layouts while avoiding obstacles or enemies.
Q Man - A Pac-Man-inspired game featuring a character collecting items in a maze while evading pursuers, originally by MRM Software.
Castle Assault - An action game where players storm a fortress, dodging defenses or enemies, also originally from MRM Software.
Banana Man - A platformer based on the British comic character Bananaman, involving collecting bananas and overcoming obstacles, another MRM title.
3D Munchy - A 3D maze game where players "munch" through a grid, avoiding hazards, considered one of MRM’s stronger offerings.

456574.overview:
Blue Ribbon Games Disc 3 is a compilation originally developed by MRM Software for the BBC Micro. The disk includes four games and one utility program: 

- Astro Plumber is an action-puzzle game where players control a character navigating a space-themed environment to fix pipes and avoid hazards. The gameplay involves moving through levels, solving pipe-connection puzzles under time pressure while dodging obstacles.

- Ravage is a space shooter game inspired by classic arcade titles like Star Wars. Players control a spaceship in a first-person perspective, navigating through space to shoot down enemy ships and projectiles. The gameplay involves managing fuel and tracking scores, as indicated by the on-screen HUD, while engaging in fast-paced combat against waves of enemies.

- Diamond Mine II is a puzzle-action game, a sequel to Diamond Mine (featured on Blue Ribbon Games Disk No. 2). Players control a character digging through a grid to collect gems while avoiding cave-ins and enemies that can end the game. The sequel introduces new levels and updated mechanics compared to the original.

- Artist is a utility program, functioning as a drawing tool. It allows players to create simple graphics and designs on the BBC Micro, serving as an early digital art application similar to basic graphic editors.

-Joey is a platform game where players control a kangaroo-like character. The gameplay involves hopping through levels to collect items and reach goals while overcoming obstacles such as gaps and enemies.

457190.overview:
Bouncer is a 1-player arcade game for the BBC Micro.

The player controls a large circle of anti-matter while Space Bouncers jump about the screen. The player has to position the circle so that Space Bouncers land in the center of the circle and are destroyed. If the Space Bouncers are not perfectly centered, the anti-matter is destroyed. The player has a limited time to destroy all bouncers on the screen. If the player loses three lives, it's game over.

457678.overview:
Gold Run is a quiz game based on the bonus round of a British quiz show Blockbusters. In this adaptation, players participate in a trivia challenge that mirrors the show's format.

In Gold Run, players navigate a board of hexagons, each containing initials corresponding to the correct answer of a trivia question. The objective is to create a path from one side of the board to the other by answering questions correctly. Incorrect answers or passes result in blocked paths, requiring players to find alternative routes. The game emphasizes quick thinking and a broad knowledge base, reflecting the fast-paced nature of the original TV segment.

This title is part of a Blockbusters-themed games released by Macsen Software.

457684.overview:
Golf is a sports simulation game for one or two players, allowing users to play either a 9-hole or 18-hole course. The layout of each hole is procedurally generated, creating a new course for each session.

The game is displayed using full-screen, full-colour graphics in a top-down perspective. Players input the direction and strength of each stroke to navigate the ball across various terrain types, including fairways, rough, greens, bunkers, and water hazards. Each shot is influenced by surface conditions and may be affected by trees, which can obscure the ball or cause unpredictable rebounds. Players are penalized for landing in water or hitting the ball out of bounds. 

The game tracks individual scores relative to par, and provides a summary on a scorecard after each hole.
